subject: POC timing playbook: sprint 4 checkpoint and acceptance runway
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Jon Park <jon.park@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC timing playbook: sprint 4 checkpoint and acceptance runway

Hi Jon —

Quick weekly checkpoint for Sprint 4 (POC trial). Below is a concise status, acceptance checkpoints we expect this week, and current blockers/asks. Aim: get to the formal acceptance runbook by next Friday so Procurement can start the PO.

Status snapshot:
- Environment: Dedicated test pool up; model variant v1.3 deployed to test GPU nodes (observed median latency 85ms for 512 tokens in nightly run).
- Traffic: Synthetic load at 60% of target throughput; customer traffic replay scheduled Tue night.
- Eval plan: v2 of the evaluation plan attached (acme-eval-plan-v2.pdf) — minor metric tweaks documented in section 2.

Acceptance criteria (targeted for 2027-05-07):
1) Functional: Top-10 customer prompts produce >=95% pass on business-rules filter (no PII leakage, correct entity normalization).
2) Quality: average rouge-L >= baseline across the curated eval set; no end-to-end regressions vs baseline >3%.
3) Performance: p95 latency <= 160ms at target concurrency; memory KPIs stable (no OOMs).
4) Ops: end-to-end telemetry shows prefix-cache hit-rate >= 40% for replay workload.

Open blockers and mitigations:
- Blocker A (ACTION): Intermittent tokenization mismatch observed on some customer prompt variants. Owner: Karthik. Mitigation: Karthik to push a tokenizer patch and run a focused 2-hour smoke run by Mon 10:00 PT.
- Blocker B: Procurement has an outstanding SSO questionnaire (attached link from Procurement). Owner: Vanessa / Jon. Mitigation: Vanessa to share SOC summary and Jon to coordinate with procurement to confirm required fields; target closure Wed EOD.
- Blocker C: TF-serving kernel fallback causing 10% tail latency spikes on long sequences. Owner: Grace. Mitigation: Grace to test kernel pinning and report results by Tue 17:00 PT.

Action items (owner / due):
- Karthik Iyer: tokenizer patch + focused smoke run (2027-05-02 10:00 PT).
- Grace O'Connor: kernel pinning tests & telemetry dump (2027-05-02 17:00 PT).
- Vanessa Ortiz: finalize acceptance checklist & send to Procurement (2027-05-04 12:00 PT).
- Jon Park (Acme): confirm final list of 10 canonical prompts and available replay window (2027-05-03 EOD).

Attachments: acme-eval-plan-v2.pdf (application/pdf), poc-telemetry-sample.csv (text/csv)

Proposed next meeting: Wed 2027-05-03 11:00 PT — 30 min sync (will send calendar invite once Jon confirms).

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
From: Jon Park <jon.park@acme-analytics.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC timing playbook: sprint 4 checkpoint and acceptance runway

Thanks Vanessa — solid summary. Quick updates from our side:
- We'll circulate the canonical 10 prompts by Tue morning (we need one additional day to lock the legal-safe variants).
- Procurement flagged the SSO questionnaire; I confirmed we only need the SOC summary and our standard SSO metadata. I can have Procurement put any missing fields in a single doc for you.
- Regarding the tokenizer mismatch: we saw the same issue in our own dev runs; if Karthik's patch looks low-risk we can fast-track it on our test replay.

One ask: our product team is seeing a small but material degradation on rollout variant A under long sequences. If you think the kernel pinning test will take longer, can we extend the POC acceptance window by +6 business days to avoid a rushed sign-off? That gives us buffer to confirm quality metrics on the full replay.

Proposed: extend acceptance target to 2027-05-13 (if Redwood agrees) and keep current cadence of checkpoints. Let me know whether that works.

—Jon
Jon Park
Principal Product Manager, Acme Analytics
jon.park@acme-analytics.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: POC timing playbook: sprint 4 checkpoint and acceptance runway

On Mon, May 3, 2027 at 08:37 AM Jon Park <jon.park@acme-analytics.com> wrote:
> One ask: our product team is seeing a small but material degradation on rollout variant A under long sequences. If you think the kernel pinning test will take longer, can we extend the POC acceptance window by +6 business days to avoid a rushed sign-off?

Vanessa / Jon — I'm running the tokenizer patch this morning; early signal looks promising. I can have a patched container and a replay run completed today. If the tokenizer fixes the majority of mismatches, that should free up cycles to focus on the kernel tail-latency issue.

On the extension ask: +6 business days (new target 2027-05-13) is reasonable from my side and reduces risk of rushed artifacts in acceptance. Operationally we can keep the same test windows and simply mark the final acceptance deadline to 5/13. If Jon confirms, I'll plan for a second smoke run across the full prompt set on Thu.

Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks everyone — alignment notes below and updated action list.

Decisions:
- Acceptance target moved to 2027-05-13 (per Jon / Karthik agreement).
- Weekly cadence remains the same; Wed 11:00 PT sync will continue.

Updated action items (owner / due):
- Karthik: complete tokenizer patch + full replay smoke run (2027-05-03 18:00 PT).
- Grace: kernel pinning investigation; if safe, schedule kernel pin for canary nodes (2027-05-05 17:00 PT).
- Vanessa: update acceptance checklist to reflect adjusted dates and share final doc with Procurement (2027-05-04 12:00 PT).
- Jon / Acme: deliver canonical 10 prompts and confirm replay window (2027-05-04 EOD).

Notes: I'll attach the updated acceptance checklist after I fold in Karthik's smoke run results. If Procurement needs any additional artifacts for SSO review, please have them send a single consolidated doc to procurement@acme-analytics.com; I'll pick it up.

Calendar: I will hold the Wed 11:00 PT slot and send a revised invite showing the new acceptance target.

Thanks —
